messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into French, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE French line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Après avoir reposé un peu mon corps fatigué, je repris la voie sur la pente déserte, de sorte que le pied ferme était toujours le plus bas.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (FR → EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|----------------------------|--------| | Poi | temporal adverb “after” | **Après** | after | OK | | ch'èi | 1st sg. perfect auxiliary “I have” (introduces the clause) | **avoir** | to have | OK | | posato | past participle “rested” | **reposé** | rested | OK | | un | indefinite article/ numeral “a” | **un** | a | OK | | poco | adverb of quantity “little” | **peu** | little | OK | | il | definite article (masc.) – “the” (here attached to *corpo*) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (French uses possessive *mon* instead) | | corpo | noun “body” | **corps** | body | OK | | lasso | adjective “weary” | **fatigué** | weary | OK | | ripresi | 1st sg. past “I resumed” | **repris** | resumed | OK | | via | noun “way, path” | **voie** | way | OK | | per | preposition “along, through” | **sur** | on/along | OK | | la | definite article (fem.) “the” (for *piaggia*) | **la** | the | OK | | piaggia | noun “slope, hillside” (archaic) | **pente** | slope | OK | | diserta | adjective “deserted, empty” | **déserte** | deserted | OK | | sì | adverb/conjunctive “so, thus” (introduces result clause) | **de** | of | OK | | che | conjunction “that” (part of result clause) | **sorte** | sort | OK | | ’l | contracted definite article “the” (masc.) | **le** | the | OK | | piè | noun “foot” (the firm foot) | **pied** | foot | OK | | fermo | adjective “firm, steady” | **ferme** | firm | OK | | sempre | adverb “always” | **toujours** | always | OK | | era | imperfect of “to be” – “was” | **était** | was | OK | | ’l (second) | contracted definite article “the” (masc.) | **le** | the | OK | | più | comparative particle “more/‑er” | **plus** | more/‑er | OK | | basso | adjective “low, lower” (comparative) | **bas** | low | OK |

### Issues Detected - **UNNECESSARY**: *il* (definite article before *corpo*). French expresses the possessive with *mon* and does not need a separate article. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** problems were found; all other source words are represented correctly and agree in gender/number with their French counterparts.
